build: TCI crack of the Firebird release, one packed file on a D64; level 1 in play

comments.text: Restores Y, X and A from the stack and returns from the interrupt.

The game's one interrupt handler, reached through the KERNAL's IRQ entry and the vector at $0314. A raster interrupt is passed to raster_dispatch; a CIA 1 timer interrupt decrements $B46B; anything else is acknowledged at the video chip and CIA 2. All three leave through irq_exit.

Acknowledges the raster interrupt, then reads the next entry of the raster list at $0E01 + $AD: a handler number, and the line for the next interrupt from $0E03, which it writes to $D012. Advances $AD by 3 and jumps through raster_handler_lo/hi. A handler number of $FF ends the list.
Low bytes of the five raster handlers: $89C4, $8AA1, $8A3E, $8A4D, $8A8C.
High bytes of the five raster handlers.
Raster handler 0. Sets the background colour to black, calls $8C9B while $8936 is non-zero, clears $AE and $A1, turns off sprites 0-5 (keeps 6 and 7) and counts frames in $1A.
Raster handler 2, entered from raster_dispatch.
Raster handler 3, entered from raster_dispatch.
Raster handler 4, entered from raster_dispatch.
Raster handler 1, entered from raster_dispatch.
Single-bit masks, $01 up to $80, one for each column of the keyboard matrix.
Message texts, each after two bytes that come before it: "Mission Complete", "No Bonus", "Planet Destroyed", "Reverse Gravity", "Invisible Landscape". Plain ASCII.
Unless $57 is non-zero, either Shift key goes on to $95E0, which calls $9339 and $9CCF; with no Shift held it jumps to $96EB.
F5 pauses the game when $27 is zero: sets $61 to 1 and waits, testing F7, until F7 is pressed, then calls $B45C and clears $61.
F1 stores $FF in $A2 (sound off); F3 stores 0 (sound on).
The keyboard matrix as read_keyboard left it: one byte per row, a set bit for each key held.
Scans the keyboard matrix: selects each of the eight rows of CIA 1 port A in turn and stores port B, inverted, in key_rows, so that a set bit is a key held down. Interrupts are off for the scan.
On a pass when $19 AND 3 is non-zero, A decrements the ship's direction in $0D and S increments it, wrapping to 0-31: 32 directions.
The same test as key_pressed, without the $63 check: always the real keyboard.

Tests one key. X is its number in the matrix, row times 8 plus column (A is $0A, S is $0D, Return $01, right Shift $34, left Shift $0F, Space $3C). Returns with Z set when the key is held. While $63 is non-zero, any key but RUN/STOP ($3F) is answered at $B49F instead of from the keyboard. What sets $63 is not known: it read 0 throughout attract mode and in play.
Key numbers of the five controls, in matrix order: A, S, Return, right Shift, Space.
The game's first instruction, reached from the crack's relocator at $6C16. Copies 13 pages from $6C47 to $4000-$4CFF, resets the stack, clears zero page from $03 to $FF, then builds tables at $0B00.
Copies three pages from $B773 to $0400-$06FF, stores 4 in $AF89 and jumps to $0400, where the copied start-up code runs.

Prints the text at $B9DD through the KERNAL's CHROUT until a $FF, then loops on $8E42 and $8DB3 until $8DB3 returns $20, and jumps to $0400. The text is the BBC Micro version's Mode 7 key page, with the crackers' credit added at its end. Nothing in the code traced so far calls this routine.

The start of three pages, $B773-$BA72, that copy_startup_to_0400 moves to $0400 and runs there: start-up code assembled for $0400, and after it data, including the names and texts below. In play $0400-$06FF hold other things, so these pages are the copy that survives. Among other things the code it sets the video bank through $DD00 and $DD02, the raster interrupt through $D01A, CIA 1's timer and the IRQ vector at $0314 (seen at $B78C-$B846 here, $0419-$04D3 as it runs).
Eight names of "SYNDICATE", padded with spaces: the high score table as this copy holds it (shown as "Top Eight Thrusters", 1000 points each).

Message texts, each a pair of bytes then the text, ended by $FF: "Game Over", "Top Eight Thrusters", "Congratulations", "Please enter your name", "Press SPACE BAR to start", "Out of fuel". Plain ASCII.

Text printed by show_bbc_keys_page, ended by $FF. It starts with 22,7, the BBC Micro's MODE 7, and uses teletext control codes ($84, $9D, $83, $8D). It reads "Jeremy's Thruster Game" (twice, for double height), "The keys are:" and the BBC version's keys (CAPS LOCK, CTRL, RETURN, SHIFT, SPACE, COPY and DELETE, Q and S, ESCAPE), then the crackers' line "Cracked By The Syndicate For TCI !" in shifted capitals and "Press the space bar to start".
